name: Kundler Klamm
kurzbeschreibung: Kundler Klamm connects the Wildschönau with the Inn Valley: a flat, accessible gorge trail along the Wildschönauer Ache featuring a stone turning workshop.
beschreibung:
Overview

The steeped-in-history Kundler Klamm is one of Tyrol's most charming and easily accessible natural gorges. It forms the natural geological link between the sunny high valley of Wildschönau near Mühltal and the market town of Kundl in the Tyrolean Unterinntal at around 530 metres above sea level. Running alongside the cheerily babbling Wildschönauer Ache river, a wide, gently sloping trail leads through a valley bordered by sheer dolomite crags. Thanks to its flat terrain, Kundler Klamm is considered an exceptionally family-friendly excursion destination.

Geology & Legendary Lore

According to legend, a terrifying dragon once dwelt in primeval Wildschönau, which was then submerged beneath a gigantic lake. A daring farmer outsmarted the monster, whereupon the dying dragon bit through the rock towards the Inntal in its death throes – the water drained away, creating the high valley and the gorge. From a geological standpoint, the Wildschönauer Ache cut through the rock over millennia, unearthing a treasure trove of colourful river gravels, conglomerates, and rare semi-precious minerals. The trail itself traces back to a historic timber-floating road: back in the 19th century, lumberjacks used the track to transport timber. In the early 20th century, the Imperial and Royal Forestry Administration expanded the road for horse-drawn wagons before it was adapted for tourism. At the valley entrance in Kundl, Tyrol's only stone turning workshop bears witness to the traditional craftsmanship of polishing gorge stones into artistic jewellery and decorative pieces.

Visit & Getting There

Kundler Klamm is freely accessible during the day throughout the snow-free months from early May to late October (officially closed in winter for safety reasons due to avalanche and rockfall hazards). Access to the gorge hiking trail is free of charge (0,00 € admission). A very popular excursion is a ride on the nostalgic slow train Bummelzug Wildschönau, which comfortably shuttles guests from the alpine village of Mühltal to the southern gorge entrance. Arrival by train: ÖBB to Kundl railway station or Wörgl railway station, from Kundl it is an approx. 20-minute signposted walk to the gorge entrance. By car: Via the Inntal motorway A12, exit Wörgl West or Kramsach, to Kundl; paid parking spaces are available at the gorge entrance (Klammstraße).

Tips

In contrast to many other Tyrolean gorges, the walking trail through Kundler Klamm runs along a wide, gravelled path without steps – making the route outstandingly suitable for pushchairs and all-terrain wheelchairs. Children love collecting and identifying the colourful pebbles on the safe riverbank. Be sure to plan a stop at the traditional inn Gasthof Kundler Klamm right by the gorge entrance on the Inntal side.
